stories.title: Kuda's rebrand trades fintech features for Lagos street life
stories.blurb: Barkas repositioned the Nigerian digital bank from challenger to established brand around the line "More Life", with geometric letterforms drawn from Nigerian art and architecture, a custom Naira sign and documentary photography shot by local photographers. Kuda's marketing lead credits the rebrand with more account openings and reactivated dormant customers, though the piece gives no figures.

sources.name: Roastbrief
sources.headline: Barkas shares distinctive new identity for Nigerian digital bank Kuda

stories.title: Marc Jacobs Beauty layers Google's video models into a real New York shoot
stories.blurb: SuperHeroes shot the campaign live with a director, crew and creator, then had the AI duo EtherealMoon add surreal city transformations with Veo for scenes and Omni for stills. A useful reference for how a hybrid production splits the work between camera and model, even if the write-up reads close to a press release.

sources.name: Roastbrief
sources.headline: Marc Jacobs Beauty, Google and SuperHeroes blend live action and Google Flow in How to New York

stories.title: Nestlé held back its food ads until sunset during Ramadan
stories.blurb: During fasting hours the campaign in Mauritius showed glasses before the pour and covered desserts under "Ready. But not yet served.", and revealed the finished dishes at Iftar. The transferable move: a cultural tension turned into the structure of the media plan, not just the copy.

sources.name: Roastbrief
sources.headline: Nestlé Looks Back at The Campaign That Waited, Its Innovative Ramadan Strategy

stories.title: Nikon strips its microscopy video winner over AI post-processing
stories.blurb: The winner of Small World in Motion admitted to AI-assisted post-processing after researchers flagged cell features that appeared and vanished and what looked like AI watermarks in the source files. Nikon handed first place to the runner-up and says it is revisiting its rules, a live case of where enhancement ends and generation begins in documentary imagery.

stories.title: Why every product ends up looking the same
stories.blurb: Luke Wroblewski lines up old and new TVs, phones and cars and sorts the usual explanations: purpose becomes clear, mature markets compete on price, physics and standards constrain form. His point for software: apps are converging on chat within a few years, where hardware took decades.
